classification.difficultyReason: Discover the equal products of opposite rectangle areas from shared dimensions, account for the unspecified placement of the three known areas and maximise over the possible arrangements.

content.prompt: A rectangle is dissected into four smaller rectangles by two straight cuts. Three of these have areas $3\text{ m}^2$, $4\text{ m}^2$ and $5\text{ m}^2$. Find the largest possible area of the fourth rectangle.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{20}{3}\text{ m}^2$.

The products of diagonally opposite areas are equal; place the missing area opposite $3\text{ m}^2$ to maximise it.
answer.worked:
The cuts form two rows and two columns. Let their heights be $h_1,h_2$ and widths be $w_1,w_2$. The products of diagonally opposite areas are equal because
$$\begin{align*}(w_1h_1)(w_2h_2)&=w_1w_2h_1h_2\\(w_1h_1)(w_2h_2)&=(w_2h_1)(w_1h_2).\end{align*}$$
The missing area can therefore be
$$\frac{3\times4}{5}=\frac{12}{5},\qquad \frac{3\times5}{4}=\frac{15}{4},\qquad \frac{4\times5}{3}=\frac{20}{3}.$$
Since $\dfrac{12}{5}<\dfrac{15}{4}<\dfrac{20}{3}$, the largest possible area is $\dfrac{20}{3}\text{ m}^2$.
